D7C1A650DFE40131272568A86D17958E.description: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which probabilities are assigned empirically; find the expected value.
comments: For example, find a current data distribution on the number of TV sets per household in the United States, and calculate the expected number of sets per household. How many TV sets would you expect to find in 100 randomly selected households?

comments: For example, find the theoretical probability distribution for the number of correct answers obtained by guessing on all five questions of a multiple-choice test where each question has four choices, and find the expected grade under various grading schemes.

D7B55B90DFE40131270368A86D17958E.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

D7B4F480DFE40131270268A86D17958E.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

D7B493C0DFE40131270168A86D17958E.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables

D7B43E40DFE40131270068A86D17958E.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. D7B3EA70DFE4013126FF68A86D17958E.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

D75A88E0DFE40131261A68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

D75A28B0DFE40131261968A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

D7587470DFE40131261568A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

D7577D10DFE40131261368A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

DAFBE430DFE401312D8768A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary of how key events or ideas develop over the course of the text.

DAFB94F0DFE401312D8668A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources, attending to such features as the date and origin of the information.

DAFAE840DFE401312D8468A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

DAFA97E0DFE401312D8368A86D17958E.description:
By the end of grade 9, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 9—10 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 10, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 9—10 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

DAFA4170DFE401312D8268A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

DAF9E5E0DFE401312D8168A86D17958E.description: Analyze seminal U.S. documents of historical and literary significance (e.g., Washington's Farewell Address, the Gettysburg Address, Roosevelt's Four Freedoms speech, King's "Letter from Birmingham Jail"), including how they address related themes and concepts.

DAF98940DFE401312D8068A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify false statements and fallacious reasoning.

DAF92080DFE401312D7F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze various accounts of a subject told in different mediums (e.g., a person's life story in both print and multimedia), determining which details are emphasized in each account.

DAF88B00DFE401312D7D68A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how an author uses rhetoric to advance that point of view or purpose.

DAF840D0DFE401312D7C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze in detail how an author's ideas or claims are developed and refined by particular sentences, paragraphs, or larger portions of a text (e.g., a section or chapter).

DAF7F4B0DFE401312D7B68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone (e.g., how the language of a court opinion differs from that of a newspaper).

DAF74080DFE401312D7968A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the author unfolds an analysis or series of ideas or events, including the order in which the points are made, how they are introduced and developed, and the connections that are drawn between them.

DAF6F090DFE401312D7868A86D17958E.description: Determine a central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the text.

DAF6A660DFE401312D7768A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

DAF5C520DFE401312D7468A86D17958E.description:
By the end of grade 9, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 9—10 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 10, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the high end of the grades 9—10 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

DAF571B0DFE401312D7368A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

DAF4DE90DFE401312D7168A86D17958E.description: Analyze how an author draws on and transforms source material in a specific work (e.g., how Shakespeare treats a theme or topic from Ovid or the Bible or how a later author draws on a play by Shakespeare).

DAF49230DFE401312D7068A86D17958E.description: Analyze the representation of a subject or a key scene in two different artistic mediums, including what is emphasized or absent in each treatment (e.g., Auden's "Musée des Beaux Arts" and Breughel's Landscape with the Fall of Icarus).

DAF3F950DFE401312D6E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze a particular point of view or cultural experience reflected in a work of literature from outside the United States, drawing on a wide reading of world literature.

DAF398D0DFE401312D6D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure a text, order events within it (e.g., parallel plots), and manipulate time (e.g., pacing, flashbacks) create such effects as mystery, tension, or surprise.

DAF34CD0DFE401312D6C68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone (e.g., how the language evokes a sense of time and place; how it sets a formal or informal tone).

DAF2B110DFE401312D6A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how complex characters (e.g., those with multiple or conflicting motivations) develop over the course of a text, interact with other characters, and advance the plot or develop the theme.

DAF25CE0DFE401312D6968A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze in detail its development over the course of the text, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the text.

DAF1F450DFE401312D6868A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

DAF0D0C0DFE401312D6568A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

DAF083C0DFE401312D6468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

DAF03330DFE401312D6368A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

DAEFDEB0DFE401312D6268A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

DAEF93B0DFE401312D6168A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

DAEEFC00DFE401312D5F68A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

DAEEAD10DFE401312D5E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

DAEE5B80DFE401312D5D68A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

DAEDA970DFE401312D5B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

DAED5D20DFE401312D5A68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

DAED0A00DFE401312D5968A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

DAEC5B10DFE401312D5768A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Connecticut Core Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

D96877D0DFE401312A4868A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).

D9682D60DFE401312A4768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).

D967E470DFE401312A4668A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

D9679A40DFE401312A4568A86D17958E.description: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.

D9674A50DFE401312A4468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

D966E200DFE401312A4368A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

D9667F60DFE401312A4268A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., telegraph, photograph, autograph).

D96636D0DFE401312A4168A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

D965EC20DFE401312A4068A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

D96555F0DFE401312A3E68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion).

D964A400DFE401312A3C68A86D17958E.description: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.

D9644BA0DFE401312A3B68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

D963A1F0DFE401312A3968A86D17958E.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

D9634740DFE401312A3868A86D17958E.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.

D962E4D0DFE401312A3768A86D17958E.description: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.

D9624EA0DFE401312A3568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

D9620560DFE401312A3468A86D17958E.description: Correctly use frequently confused words (e.g., to, too, two; there, their).

D961B7C0DFE401312A3368A86D17958E.description: Produce complete sentences, recognizing and correcting inappropriate fragments and run-ons.

D960F560DFE401312A3168A86D17958E.description: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns (e.g., a small red bag rather than a red small bag).

D960AEA0DFE401312A3068A86D17958E.description: Use modal auxiliaries (e.g., can, may, must) to convey various conditions.

D9606770DFE401312A2F68A86D17958E.description: Form and use the progressive (e.g., I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.

D9602030DFE401312A2E68A86D17958E.description: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why).

D95FD640DFE401312A2D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

D95EE1E0DFE401312A2A68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

D95E9670DFE401312A2968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

D95E47D0DFE401312A2868A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

D95DA350DFE401312A2668A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

D95CF970DFE401312A2468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

D95CAE50DFE401312A2368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

D95C0250DFE401312A2168A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

D95B9B70DFE401312A2068A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

D95B25F0DFE401312A1F68A86D17958E.description: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

D95AD260DFE401312A1E68A86D17958E.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.

D95A3A20DFE401312A1C68A86D17958E.description: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.

D959E2B0DFE401312A1B68A86D17958E.description: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

D9599B00DFE401312A1A68A86D17958E.description: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

D9595130DFE401312A1968A86D17958E.description: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.

D9590740DFE401312A1868A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

D958BC30DFE401312A1768A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

D9586A50DFE401312A1668A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

D9575EA0DFE401312A1368A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

D95708B0DFE401312A1268A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

D956B0E0DFE401312A1168A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

D9560B20DFE401312A0F68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

D955B9E0DFE401312A0E68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

D9555A40DFE401312A0D68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

D954C0C0DFE401312A0B68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

D95468F0DFE401312A0A68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

D953D6A0DFE401312A0868A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to informational texts (e.g., "Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text").

D9538930DFE401312A0768A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text [e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions].").

D9533890DFE401312A0668A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

D952E700DFE401312A0568A86D17958E.description: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.

D9528D50DFE401312A0468A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.

D9523B00DFE401312A0368A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

D951E7D0DFE401312A0268A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of one page in a single sitting.

D9519290DFE401312A0168A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.

D95145B0DFE401312A0068A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
comments: (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1—3 above.)

D9509930DFE4013129FE68A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

D9504910DFE4013129FD68A86D17958E.description: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.

D94FDDB0DFE4013129FC68A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.

D94F7E80DFE4013129FB68A86D17958E.description: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.

D94F30C0DFE4013129FA68A86D17958E.description: Orient the reader by establishing a situationand introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

D94EDFE0DFE4013129F968A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

D94E8E90DFE4013129F868A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented

D94E39A0DFE4013129F768A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

D94DE5B0DFE4013129F668A86D17958E.description: Link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases (e.g., another, for example, also, because).

D94D8AE0DFE4013129F568A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.

D94D2DB0DFE4013129F468A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

D94CD810DFE4013129F368A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

D94C82D0DFE4013129F268A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

D94C3400DFE4013129F168A86D17958E.description: Link opinion and reasons using words and phrases (e.g., for instance, in order to, in addition).

D94BE3B0DFE4013129F068A86D17958E.description: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.

D94B8540DFE4013129EF68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped to support the writer's purpose.

D94B1D60DFE4013129EE68A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information

D949B680DFE4013129EB68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

D9492320DFE4013129E968A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

D948DA70DFE4013129E868A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

D94890F0DFE4013129E768A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

D9484340DFE4013129E668A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

D947CE60DFE4013129E568A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

D9477990DFE4013129E468A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

D9472770DFE4013129E368A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

D9469380DFE4013129E168A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

D9464180DFE4013129E068A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

D945E1C0DFE4013129DF68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

D9455170DFE4013129DD68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

D94506D0DFE4013129DC68A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

D944B170DFE4013129DB68A86D17958E.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings

D9444A90DFE4013129DA68A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

D943F630DFE4013129D968A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

D9436710DFE4013129D768A86D17958E.description: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.

D9431CB0DFE4013129D668A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

D9422650DFE4013129D368A86D17958E.description: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 4—5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

D941DFC0DFE4013129D268A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

D94198F0DFE4013129D168A86D17958E.description: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.

D94150C0DFE4013129D068A86D17958E.description: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.

D9410670DFE4013129CF68A86D17958E.description: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively (e.g., in charts, graphs, diagrams, time lines, animations, or interactive elements on Web pages) and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of the text in which it appears.

D9405540DFE4013129CD68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic; describe the differences in focus and the information provided.

D93FFEB0DFE4013129CC68A86D17958E.description: Describe the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.

D93FA9E0DFE4013129CB68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in a text relevant to a grade 4 topic or subject area.

D93EF040DFE4013129C968A86D17958E.description: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on specific information in the text.

D93E73E0DFE4013129C868A86D17958E.description: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize the text.

D93E2B50DFE4013129C768A86D17958E.description: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

D93D4610DFE4013129C468A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, in the grades 4—5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

D93CF990DFE4013129C368A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

D93CA0B0DFE4013129C268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics (e.g., opposition of good and evil) and patterns of events (e.g., the quest) in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.

D93C5560DFE4013129C168A86D17958E.description: Make connections between the text of a story or drama and a visual or oral presentation of the text, identifying where each version reflects specific descriptions and directions in the text.

D93B6590DFE4013129BE68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.

D93B0AF0DFE4013129BD68A86D17958E.description: Explain major differences between poems, drama, and prose, and refer to the structural elements of poems (e.g., verse, rhythm, meter) and drama (e.g., casts of characters, settings, descriptions, dialogue, stage directions) when writing or speaking about a text.

D93AAAE0DFE4013129BC68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including those that allude to significant characters found in mythology (e.g., Herculean).

D93A13E0DFE4013129BA68A86D17958E.description: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions).

D939C490DFE4013129B968A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize the text.

D9396930DFE4013129B868A86D17958E.description: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

D9386310DFE4013129B568A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

D937C850DFE4013129B368A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

D9377B30DFE4013129B268A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

D91AAFE0DFE4013129A568A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships (e.g., After dinner that night we went looking for them).

D919FEA0DFE4013129A368A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).

D919A2C0DFE4013129A268A86D17958E.description: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).

D9194FE0DFE4013129A168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

D9190310DFE4013129A068A86D17958E.description: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

D918B390DFE40131299F68A86D17958E.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company, companion).

D91845B0DFE40131299E68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).

D917CD00DFE40131299D68A86D17958E.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

D9177C90DFE40131299C68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning word and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

D916DA50DFE40131299A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard English.

D9168820DFE40131299968A86D17958E.description: Choose words and phrases for effect.

D9162CD0DFE40131299868A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

D9159D50DFE40131299668A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

D91553C0DFE40131299568A86D17958E.description: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.

D914F8F0DFE40131299468A86D17958E.description: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, happiness).

D9143720DFE40131299268A86D17958E.description: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.

D9135680DFE40131298F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

D9130A70DFE40131298E68A86D17958E.description: Produce simple, compound, and complex sentences.

D91153B0DFE40131298968A86D17958E.description: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.

D910A280DFE40131298768A86D17958E.description: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.

D9105730DFE40131298668A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in general and their functions in particular sentences.

D9100A50DFE40131298568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

D90F1050DFE40131298268A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

D90EC750DFE40131298168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

D90E7E40DFE40131298068A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

D90DE850DFE40131297E68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

D90D3580DFE40131297C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

D90CDF40DFE40131297B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

D9059A50DFE40131296768A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

D90549A0DFE40131296668A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

D904FA60DFE40131296568A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

document.title: Connecticut Science Curriculum Grade-Level Expectations

D30615C0DFE401311E4868A86D17958E.description: Calculate potential and kinetic energy and relate those quantities to total energy in a system.

D3083C40DFE401311E5068A86D17958E.description: Trace energy conversions that occur in the human body once food enters and explain the conversions in writing.

D307F9F0DFE401311E4F68A86D17958E.description: Discuss different forms of energy and describe how they can be converted from one form to another for use by humans (e.g., thermal, electrical, light, chemical, mechanical).

D307B570DFE401311E4E68A86D17958E.description: Use a diagram or model of a moving object (roller coaster, pendulum, etc.) to describe the conversion of potential energy into kinetic energy and vice versa.

D3075AF0DFE401311E4D68A86D17958E.description: Design and create a working compound machine from several simple machines.

D3071270DFE401311E4C68A86D17958E.description: Defend the statement, "Work output of a machine is always less than work input because of energy lost due to friction."

D306D580DFE401311E4B68A86D17958E.description: Determine ways to modify a simple machine (inclined plane, pulley and lever) to improve its mechanical advantage.

D30694F0DFE401311E4A68A86D17958E.description: Explain in writing how the six simple machines make work easier but do not alter the amount of work done on an object, and demonstrate how everyday objects function as simple machines

D30654B0DFE401311E4968A86D17958E.description: Calculate work done on an object as force or distance varies.

D305D830DFE401311E4768A86D17958E.description: Conduct simple experiments that show and explain how forces work to change the motion of an object.

D3059710DFE401311E4668A86D17958E.description: Energy provides the ability to do work and can exist in many forms.

D302D410DFE401311E3C68A86D17958E.description: Label the major parts of the human digestive system and explain in writing the function of each part in the chemical and physical breakdown of food (mouth, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine and rectum).

D3050E10DFE401311E4468A86D17958E.description: Design and conduct controlled variable experiments to analyze the interaction between the circulatory and respiratory systems as the demand for oxygen changes.

D304CE70DFE401311E4368A86D17958E.description: Label the major parts of the human circulatory system and explain in writing the function of each part (heart, veins, arteries and capillaries).

D3048F00DFE401311E4268A86D17958E.description: Label the major parts of the human respiratory system and explain in writing the function of each part (nasal cavity, trachea, bronchi, lungs and diaphragm).

D3044BA0DFE401311E4168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how the muscles, tendons, ligaments and bones interact to support the human body and allow movement.

D3040570DFE401311E4068A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between the structures and range of motion associated with ball, socket and hinge joints and relate human joints to simple machines.

D303B9F0DFE401311E3F68A86D17958E.description: Investigate and explain in writing the basic structure and function of the human skeletal system.

D30365C0DFE401311E3E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the structure and function of multicellular organisms (animals) depends on the interaction of cells, tissues, organs and organ systems.

D3031E90DFE401311E3D68A86D17958E.description: Illustrate and describe in writing the structure and the functions of the following: cell membrane, cytoplasm, mitochondria and nucleus of an animal cell.

D3028F20DFE401311E3B68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast single-celled organisms with multicellular organisms.

D3024470DFE401311E3A68A86D17958E.description: Many organisms, including humans, have specialized organ systems that interact with each other to maintain dynamic internal balance.

D3019E00DFE401311E3868A86D17958E.description: Evaluate and report how each method of food preservation including dehydration, pickling, irradiation and refrigeration works to stop or inhibit bacterial growth and give examples of each.

D3015FB0DFE401311E3768A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the role of bacteria in food production and food spoilage.

D3012140DFE401311E3668A86D17958E.description: Discover and discuss how humans use bacteria to produce food and identify examples.

D300E200DFE401311E3568A86D17958E.description: Illustrate and describe the structural differences between bacterial and animal cells.

D300A330DFE401311E3468A86D17958E.description: Describe the optimum conditions for rapid bacterial growth.

D3006320DFE401311E3368A86D17958E.description: Investigate and describe in writing different types of microbes and the environmental conditions necessary for their survival.

D3001E10DFE401311E3268A86D17958E.description:
Technology allows us to improve food production and preservation, thus improving our ability to meet the nutritional needs of growing populations.
This content standard is an application of the concepts in content standard 7.2 and should be integrated into the same unit.

D2FD60F0DFE401311E2868A86D17958E.description: Observe and report on the geological events that are responsible for having shaped Connecticut's landscape.

D2FF5DC0DFE401311E2F68A86D17958E.description: Investigate and determine how glaciers form and affect the Earth's surface as they change over time.

D2FF21D0DFE401311E2E68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the major agents of erosion and deposition of sediments: running water, moving ice, wave action, wind and mass movement due to gravity.

D2FEE4A0DFE401311E2D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and interpret data about the location, frequency and intensity of earthquakes.

D2FEA480DFE401311E2C68A86D17958E.description: Compare geological features that result from constructive forces (e.g., mountains and ridges) with geological features that result from destructive forces (e.g., canyons and flood plains).

D2FE4730DFE401311E2B68A86D17958E.description: Correlate common geological features/events (deep sea trenches, mountains, earthquakes, volcanoes) with the location of plate boundaries.

D2FDEE90DFE401311E2A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the processes of folding and faulting of the Earth's crust.

D2FDA990DFE401311E2968A86D17958E.description: Explain how Earth's internal energy is transferred to move tectonic plates.

D2FD1EE0DFE401311E2768A86D17958E.description: Illustrate and describe in writing the composition of the three major layers of the Earth's interior.
