document.title: Connecticut Elementary and Secondary Social Studies Standards

BB42CDD09A2147B3BCE23F6C680E4098.description:
Analyze the impact of multimedia on American politics and public discourse (e.g., 24-hour
news cycle, echo chambers, social media algorithms, live streaming, trolls, deep fakes,
artificial intelligence).

1B127DD939E944E3A02F2002B7B1DE99.description:
Analyze the impact of personal perspectives in public debates about national security and
individual liberties (e.g., 2nd Amendment, Obergefell v. Hodges, Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s
Health Organization, Sanctuary Cities, Dakota Access Pipeline).

F21F835202F3420288649E94ED25D212.description:
Evaluate the effects of human-made and natural catastrophes on global trade, politics, and
human migration in the United States (e.g., Hurricane Katrina, Flint water crisis, Deepwater
Horizon oil spill, climate change, investments in green technology).

1598B5CA5C584C7B86BCA47B891E324E.description:
Describe domestic economic policies in terms of market outcomes (e.g., North American
Free Trade Agreement, Electronic Benefit Transfer, Great Recession, Dodd-Frank Wall Street
Reform and Consumer Protection Act, Puerto Rico Oversight, Management, and Economic
Stability Act).

90AB2043280D42CF882DC82E7A336D5B.description:
Analyze how the September 11th attacks shaped perspectives in the United States (e.g.,
views of Muslims and Sikhs, Department of Homeland Security, Transportation Security
Administration, Patriot Act).

EC15EAC9F41642FA869F93EC54921762.description:
Analyze the multiple and complex causes and effects of the September 11th attacks on
domestic and foreign policy.

958C1700A7D94ECFBC67BC326BF6F216.description:
Analyze the effectiveness of individual and group responses to public policies that they
deem to be discriminatory.

1D25DB73E21A40758BCACA694655074F.description: Assess the US response to human rights violations around the world (e.g., genocide, support for free elections, sanctions, humanitarian aid, funds for human rights organizations).

91F54633A96744398C41C4D1FC39CC9B.description: National Identity in the Digital Age

C4FF239E07424CB093FA8558D45B6594.description:
Evaluate United States policies to address public safety in terms of intended and
unintended outcomes, and related consequences (e.g., War on Drugs, “America Responds
to AIDS” public information campaign, Immigration Reform and Control Act).

6D59B103BFEF4736A82D005B94E1CB9D.description:
Analyze changing spatial patterns of cultural enclaves within and among United States
regions using paper-based and electronic graphic techniques (e.g., Jamaican, Puerto Rican,
Bosnian, Vietnamese, Sikh, Mexican, Cuban, Muslim).

A19D935215BB49428D11A71D798D2317.description:
Develop an argument about the long-term causes and triggering events of United States
foreign policies designed to contain and dismantle communism (e.g., Iran Hostage Crisis, El
Salvador, Nicaragua, Iran-Contra, Afghanistan).

7B50B91A63104C329CEC12EB593AB336.description:
Analyze how innovations in the application of technology contributed to cultural and
political diffusion (e.g., televangelism, Music Television, personal computing, Hip Hop music,
cable television, political talk radio).

48470410861E4BBE97A2C3513E100462.description: Evaluate how popular culture in the 1970s and 1980s promoted and reflected hyperconsumerism, racial tension, women’s empowerment, and the Cold War.

1FA636AEBA8A4D4E80F66BA05C4422EF.description:
Evaluate whether the conservative ascendency of the 1980s was a reaction to social and
economic change and to what extent it was consistent with broader historical trends (e.g.,
New Right, Watergate, energy crisis, Reaganomics).

3C520AAFC6894AD29F59E609433DEC6D.description: Foreign Policy, Global Conflicts and Cultural Shifts

0BB604F0B91442E79FD94E992DD679F2.description:
Determine the usefulness of historical sources to support an inquiry about the causes,
escalation, and public reaction to the Vietnam War based on their maker, origin, intended
audience, and purpose (e.g., art, ephemera, film, government reports, media, music).

5759C5DEC65C43D8A3D3EAB130D1944B.description:
Analyze the role of legislative and judicial decisions in expanding or limiting civil liberties
(e.g., Hernandez v. Texas, Executive Order 10450, Loving v. Virginia, Civil Rights Act of 1964,
Voting Rights Act of 1965, Title IX of the Education Amendments Act of 1972, Roe v. Wade).

701B13CC05244FBEAA235AE8FE36E494.description:
Evaluate the effectiveness of individuals, groups, and institutions in addressing issues of
civil rights and justice in the post-World War II era (e.g., disability, education, environmental
justice, LGBTQ+ rights, poverty, racial and gender equity, voting access).

4D8CE78C9A8C4EA4B7C92C0F7AA822DC.description:
Identify both long term causes and triggering events to develop historical arguments about
efforts to abolish legalized racial segregation, discrimination, and disenfranchisement
(e.g., Southern Christian Leadership Conference, Black Panther Party, Student Nonviolent
Coordinating Committee, American Jewish Congress, American Indian Movement, United
Farm Workers, Congress of Racial Equality).

6C0B1439F60D41E19EF3245AB506647B.description:
Analyze the role of popular culture, subculture, and counterculture in shaping public
perception of national identity during the post-World War II era (e.g., Beat Generation, Rock
and Roll, Motown, Jazz, Hippies, television sitcoms, Hollywood films).

7FB734EC2AAA4268B296B0DAA46A87CB.description:
Develop a reasoned argument about the role of the United States government in providing
access to fair and open housing using multiple relevant sources (e.g., Federal Housing
Administration, Servicemen’s Readjustment Act of 1944, Levittown, redlining, Interstate
Highway System).

99CE2E2BCC354C5DB164EB53AF97444B.description:
Explain why investments in infrastructure and industry expanded consumer culture and
increased standards of living in the United States (e.g., housing access, mass production,
urbanization, utilities).

C41431B2A9CF403884130DF41E56062E.description:
Analyze how heightened domestic tensions and claims about perceived threats to
democratic values led to widespread civil rights violations (e.g., House Un-American Activities
Committee, Hollywood Ten, Lavender Scare, treatment of Civil Rights and anti-Vietnam War
activists, televised news).

093BAE91C07F464BB730A17B8BBA13EF.description:
Evaluate how the Korean and Vietnam Wars were products of the geopolitical contexts of the
Cold War.

7D18880F73A6476FBECB24C7F1BB167D.description:
Evaluate the impact of foreign policy and military intervention in upholding the United States’
founding ideals during the Cold War (e.g., Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, North Atlantic
Treaty Organization, Warsaw Pact, Korea, Cuba, Chile, Vietnam).

F54663B97B514FD99F8C3630B2360B30.description:
Analyze the multiple and complex causes and effects of the nuclear age (e.g., Manhattan
Project, Hiroshima, Nagasaki, Operation Paperclip, nuclear proliferation, Strategic Arms
Limitations Treaties, atomic culture, Three Mile Island accident).

A97C86093B2E43D4B3F226CCA9D94281.description:
Evaluate the United States government’s complex responses to the Holocaust while
recognizing the history of antisemitism in both historical and contemporary contexts (e.g.,
Voyage of the St. Louis, lack of response to the Final Solution, Nuremberg Trials).

49EB8009D5CA4AF582BD1E4D37462500.description:
Evaluate how the demand for labor on homefront in World War II shaped gender roles (e.g.,
mobilization, victory gardens, rationing, War Production Board).

3453C1561143447AB6FD05AE9D3AE469.description:
Describe the achievements and contributions of diverse individuals and groups during
World War II using evidence from historical sources (e.g., Women accepted for Volunteer
Emergency Service, Tuskegee Airman, Navajo Code Talkers, 442 Japanese-American
regiment, 158th Regimental Combat Team).

0154EA580B7A4AC2A03623C4225D305D.description:
Develop arguments about the juxtaposition between the United States’ founding ideals and
actions of the Federal government during World War II using evidence from multiple relevant
sources (e.g., Japanese-American Internment, Holocaust intervention, Braceros Program, Fair
Employment Practices Act, segregated regiments, women in the military).

82DB32656D4243E098FC089FC1AF8F41.description:
Evaluate the role of economic and political developments that created the conditions leading
to WWII and the Holocaust (e.g., Great Depression, nationalism, militarism).

407911B560D54BCEA6F9504FCCEE361D.description:
Describe the possible consequences, both intended and unintended, of government
policies to address social and economic problems during the Great Depression (e.g., role
of the Federal government, banking practices, inequitable access to benefits, migration,
environmental impacts, social safety net).

06E35AF618744B6C9519F5D72DDFC54B.description:
Explain potential approaches to stabilize markets in response to the Great Depression (e.g.,
plans by Herbert Hoover, Franklin D. Roosevelt, Huey Long, and the American Communist
Party).

8955DB218DA94552A7F8C2CE7CDA05C8.description: Analyze the ways in which government incentives and personal motivation influenced production and distribution under New Deal policies (e.g., Agricultural Adjustment Act, Tennessee Valley Authority Act, Civilian Conservation Corps, Federal Housing Administration).

6F6EEAECA9834437920FC895E975768D.description:
Develop questions to investigate the causes and effects of the Great Depression using
multiple historical sources.

4772CE8B775A48DD92B50DD215380127.description:
Analyze how authors, artists, and musicians documented perspectives and experiences of
individuals and groups throughout the interwar period (e.g., Jacob Lawrence, Dorthea Lange,
Langston Hughes, Billie Holiday, Yasuo Kuniyoshi, Magdalena Carmen Frida Kahlo y Calderón).

BB0763E8066543D0B905D2789B67E37B.description:
Analyze the causes and effects of the Great Migration (e.g., Jim Crow laws, racial terrorism,
emergence of urban Black cultural centers, resurgence of Islam).

7ABFA4DD8EF64C1B82E37B317751EE77.description:
Analyze the role of citizens in advocating for and ratifying the 19th Amendment to the United
States Constitution (e.g., Ida B. Wells, Alice Paul, Anna Bernard Shaw, Helena Hill Weed, Frank
B. Brandegee).

73E0209172E449D88930C1722F32A69A.description:
Analyze complex and interacting factors that influenced a debate over national identity in the
United States in the 1920s (e.g., Scopes Trial, Jazz, flappers, Immigration Act of 1924, Marcus
Garvey, mass media and advertising).

88AF04A1F1514DEAA52A7A401AAD5545.description:
Analyze how racism and nativism shaped perspectives about individuals and groups and
influenced government policy (e.g., Red Summer, Sacco Vanzetti, eugenics movement,
immigration acts in the 1920s, Angel Island, Ku Klux Klan).

FA96805900DC4C8DAFE12420ADD3BC2C.description: The 1920s, Great Depression, and New Deal

5F86F77B2B4C437FAAC05477134E3B82.description:
Evaluate the juxtaposition between celebration of wartime service in World War I and the
discrimination faced by individuals and groups using evidence from multiple historical sources
(e.g., European, Latino, Indigenous, and Black service members, Thind v. United States).

B1BE7C4C835C45A1B49E3F02DD08FFF9.description:
Analyze how advancements in warfare impacted military personnel and civilians (e.g., aircraft,
artillery, chemical weapons, land mines, trench warfare, shell shock).

AA2691DD59924D25A64D561539D03FD2.description:
Analyze the causes and effects of United States involvement in WWI (e.g., threats to United
States neutrality, support for democracy, suppression of civil liberties, debate over the
League of Nations and the United States role in global affairs).

5F1ABCD45C2C44C895327AD48D2F97F5.description:
Analyze how economic and cultural hegemony influenced American perspectives of
imperialism at the end of the 19th century (e.g., Cuba, Puerto Rico, Spanish-American
War, Annexation of Hawaii and Philippines, dispossession of Latino American lands in the
American West).

038D83C37D864BB092446ED1DFDFDEC0.description:
Evaluate the role of the media in shaping public opinions and debates about America’s
emergence as an imperial power (e.g., muckrakers, yellow journalism, propaganda).

18F627757AC841E190958B46BAF1925A.description:
Analyze how people in the Progressive Era used and challenged laws to advance social,
political, economic, and environmental reforms (e.g., Populist Party, B’nai B’rith, National
Woman Suffrage Movement, Sierra Club, Niagara Movement, Socialist Party of America).

068527DB995C4DCE89207B61E9027A50.description: Evaluate how the Progressive Era is a result of immigration and industrialization (e.g., antilynching, Settlement House Movement, improved working conditions, childrens’ rights).

5B23045F3C8F4DA6816C5A3FF581C4C0.description:
Describe how individual and group perspectives about gender and sexuality in the late
19th and early 20th centuries are documented in historical records while noting possible
limitations (e.g., We’wha, Vaudeville, bicycles, women’s suffrage and education).

3A9599E288524B138AE0FE2249F2F7FD.description:
Evaluate the impact of laissez-faire economic policies regarding corporate decision making,
labor conditions, and public advocacy in the Gilded Age (e.g., monopoly, captains of industry,
muckrakers, social Darwinism, labor unions).

C9EC435A48064748A9B36D81A4B02196.description:
Develop questions about the rise of nativism and assimilation efforts of immigrants and
Indigenous peoples (e.g., Punjabi Migration, Indian Boarding Schools, Chinese Exclusion Act,
Rock Spring Massacre, 1907 Bellingham Riots, Immigration Act of 1917).

FB35E012A0074CB589042172AE660F66.description:
Analyze complex and interacting factors that influenced the strategies for Black social and
economic progress in the late 19th and early 20th centuries (e.g., Booker T. Washington,
W.E.B. Du Bois, Ida B. Wells, Mary Townsend Seymour).

DC415249029D4E53A6BB2C44786DF2D1.description:
Explain how contemporary perspectives of Reconstruction are shaped by political and social
attitudes.

E8AC359CE828495CB7C787A678FADA59.description:
Analyze the historical context of racism, racial violence, and challenges to reconciliation
between the United States and the former Confederacy.

B322AFEC9AD1424CB5F30FFF68D74E8E.description:
Evaluate the effectiveness of state and federal government in upholding the Reconstruction
Amendments (e.g., Black Codes, Enforcement Acts, Jim Crow laws).

3D2AC312A13E409695D0BFAF5E842CF4.description:
Evaluate intended and unintended outcomes of Reconstruction plans and policies in terms of
rebuilding a shared national identity (e.g., Radical Republicans, Compromise of 1877,
Freedmen’s Bureau, Reconstruction Treaties).

8B950719BA4042C2A81BF9CF9DE1AECE.description:
Analyze the political, economic, and social agency demonstrated by Black Americans
throughout the period of Reconstruction using evidence from multiple relevant historical
sources (e.g., Black Republicans, Historically Black Colleges and Universities, Edisto Island).

B978BF32C34B42409ADE1F4066DCE43C.description:
Evaluate and implement strategies for individual and collective action to address
national problems in classrooms, schools, and out-of-school civic contexts.

B750A17CE3A84E14BF6241C0EAE1A93A.description:
Analyze the characteristics and causation of national problems issues, both past and
present, using a multidisciplinary lens.

E9F7CDD0604B490986802478096EC6D4.description:
Present arguments and explanations that feature evocative ideas and multiple
perspectives about United States History topics to reach a range of audiences and
venues outside the classroom using print, oral, and digital technologies.

7D2FD5F5BE1C4DC0816BADF70DD9E32A.description:
Critique historical arguments and explanations while acknowledging the strengths
and weaknesses given the purpose and audience (e.g., credibility, bias, reasoning,
sequencing, details).

40C1A93CFAC94AF48D9798FD6DBA1418.description:
Construct explanations using sound reasoning, correct sequence, relevant examples,
and pertinent details to contextualize evidence and arguments (e.g., chronology,
causation, procedure).

CF38932D8ABB478684135D7AB7A28057.description:
Construct arguments using precise and knowledgeable claims, with evidence from
multiple sources, while acknowledging counterclaims and evidentiary weaknesses.

EDA5AE9EA807475CAFCCD1ED6E4E3A82.description: Communicate Conclusions and Take Informed Action

8588235AC0EA4A819B15F6152D77AB46.description:
Refine claims and counterclaims by pointing out strengths and limitations of arguments
and explanations (e.g., precision, significance, knowledge conveyed).

D357FBDCBF6D4C46A06EFC3A6C9D5826.description:
Organize and prioritize evidence directly and substantively from multiple sources in
order to develop or strengthen claims (e.g., detect inconsistencies).

38CA880A621647AF9F61B6F8CE4BF0FA.description:
Gather relevant information from multiple sources representing a wide range of views
and mediums while using the origin, authority, structure, context, and corroborative
value to guide the selection of credible sources.

1FD769E8BB7E4F91B6AF9085E24B60AC.description:
Apply disciplinary knowledge and practices to demonstrate an understanding of United
States history content.

14FE9033DEA744A3ACC2883C7BFC3173.description:
Determine the kinds of sources that will be helpful in answering compelling and
supporting questions, taking into consideration multiple points of view represented in the
sources, the types of sources available, and the potential uses of the sources.

A19B00B669E945A385DA1DB9E71DFFE8.description:
Explain how supporting questions contribute to an inquiry and how new compelling and
supporting questions emerge when engaging sources that represent varied perspectives.

F3B0F93A6C274ABEBD373AF6F6D5A557.description:
Explain how compelling and supporting questions reflect an enduring issue in United
States History.

document.title: Connecticut Elementary and Secondary Social Studies Standards

B55EC049D5744B9A89B9883F922571E6.description: Analyze how social contexts shape personal political beliefs and voting behavior.

37A7E81C6A954B70BEC128C1246DAFC7.description:
Evaluate the role of the media in addressing social and political problems or influencing
elections (e.g., fourth estate, media bias, concentration of media ownership).

44D0A6C628994A809F0FEA5CB2E64A1C.description:
Evaluate the effectiveness of strategies used by an individual, group or institution in
addressing a social problem at the local, state, tribal, national, and/or international level
(e.g., social protest movements, get-out-the-vote campaigns, conscious consumerism).

D9AA742D5A564C6FAD989EA6710C022B.description:
Analyze the rights and responsibilities of individuals in the United States (e.g., 4th
Amendment, trial by jury, jury service, interacting with law enforcement, voting).

B0E543F8F30140CF8919CE415BFF412A.description:
Analyze trends in access to voting, voter turnout, and voter representation over time (e.g.,
gerrymandering, reapportionment, redistricting, voter socialization).

A3D4D9A56AA249D7B4D8CD4151DFDFF0.description:
Determine the extent to which elected officials represent constituent interests and
perspectives (e.g., personal and professional experiences, policy positions, party affiliation,
voting record).

A18DF4DE59F7429EA8B4A1B6A41F667F.description:
Analyze the role of individuals, groups, and the media in shaping political participation over
time in the United States (e.g., interest groups, media bias, political parties).

FA91049D67044A60AB64BC3E26788FAD.description:
Analyze how historical contexts have shaped and continue to shape the ideologies and
platforms of political parties in the United States (e.g., factions, partisanship).

BB85FF899E0B4CCAB44751A6E3BC10E5.description:
Describe the roles of the executive branch in developing and implementing economic
policies in the United States (e.g., Department of the Treasury, Federal Reserve Board,
Internal Revenue Service).

0499A32268E040B79D78A45C3AA3D7DD.description:
Evaluate a United States trade policy in terms of costs and benefits (e.g., sanctions,
subsidies, tariffs, trade agreements, employment).

AC8DBD4B371C47388404A937C6C2249A.description:
Analyze the impact of United States policy decisions on other nations (e.g., immigration,
trade, arms support, sanctions).

B5A2169393FA4AA789F4B1A68A7D67DD.description:
Evaluate how a regulation or law can create or eliminate systemic inequalities involving
race, gender and sexuality, ability, socio-economic status, belief systems, or access to
resources (e.g., gerrymandering, 14th Amendment, Plessy v. Ferguson, poll taxes, Sheff v.
O’Neill, Voting Rights Act of 1965, Rehabilitation Act).

DCCB4048504C49B190010928CD70A1AD.description:
Critique geopolitical relationships and their impact on governments, civil societies, and/
or economic markets (e.g., North Atlantic Treaty Organization, United States–Mexico–
Canada Agreement, Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, Paris Agreement, World Health
Organization).

EF53AFCA04D94D59BB755CDBCA6402A1.description:
Evaluate the relationship between law-making, enforcement, and interpretation in balancing
the rights of the individual with the well being of society (e.g., Bill of Rights, Supreme Court
cases).

53FC0309635D4126A1396583F7CE0A72.description:
Analyze how federal and state court systems are articulated and maintained by
constitutions and laws in the United States (e.g., District Courts, Circuit Courts, Appellate
Court, Supreme Court).

E5849EBB30C649C6AEC7DEBFC86E3E80.description:
Analyze how elections and the electoral process are executed and maintained by
constitutions and laws in the United States (e.g., voter registration, transfer of power,
Electoral College, federalism).

CCDD400AEAEE4FC496BF33A325A6DB57.description:
Analyze the role and effectiveness of the legislative branch in addressing constituent and
societal needs (e.g., Article I, Section 8 of the United States Constitution, elections, political
polling, representation, constituent services).

D9A0529D3BEB4F64992AEB1366C2398E.description:
Analyze how the United States' structures of state and local governments represent
different models of democracy (e.g., direct democracy, representative government).

9FB6C692B40F44828F8B10DF71956DBC.description:
Distinguish between the powers and responsibilities of local, state, and federal election
officials in facilitating free and fair election processes.

6E37B85E8D10463C9119BCFCE1EE4233.description:
Distinguish between the functions of local, state, tribal, and national governments in
response to challenges (e.g., court decisions, executive orders, legislation, sovereignty,
states’ rights).

D457CC2DE048442FA12A21382C787464.description:
Analyze advocacy and activism in the United States related to a contemporary human rights
issue using the United States Constitution and other historical sources (e.g., youth activism,
journalism, social media, whistleblowers, protestors, strikes, boycotts, petitions, resistance).

C62375AAF1A44E2198C69747466054FA.description:
Analyze historical, contemporary, and emerging means of protecting, defending, and
promoting constitutional rights in the United States (e.g., law-making, federal court system,
constitutional amendments, Supreme Court decisions, exercising constitutional rights).

9C126629BC3B41F693A16C1A6B170FF8.description:
Evaluate how different levels of government work to promote civic virtue and enact
democratic principles (e.g., municipal, state, and federal).

CE3C80B079584AD0A4CCE3609A20E43E.description:
Identify how the structure of state and local governments promote democratic principles
and public participation (e.g., boards of education, Connecticut General Assembly, municipal
government).

C0973BFDCD3D46658415EE24B7E0F5A0.description:
Explain how federalism led to conflict between states and the federal government (e.g.,
healthcare, suffrage, taxation).

AB8525DDC43F4A7B99AD96A207DA2441.description:
Explain how the United States Constitution has been adapted and interpreted in response
to societal changes in both historical and contemporary contexts (e.g., amendments, Marbury v. Madison, Brown v. Board of Education, Tinker v. DesMoines, Obergefell v. Hodges).

78D2017DE82746D1A3F9D2E25C24692C.description:
Describe how the United States Constitution organizes, enumerates, and divides power to
create a limited government (e.g., separation of powers, checks and balances, necessary
and proper clause, supremacy clause, 10th Amendment).

F5750FC2F154451EA8607BC3B79FAADB.description:
Explain how the Declaration of Independence and United States Constitution contributed to
the establishment of a federal democratic republic (e.g., popular sovereignty, federalism).

996D25310E3F47D29B59026C2497FA9F.description:
Analyze how interpretations of the social contract theory of government influenced the
founding of the United States government (e.g., Thomas Hobbes, Jean-Jacques Rousseau,
John Locke).

B1F2DE39426341AAA5D87938D9C75124.description:
Evaluate and implement strategies for individual and collective action to address local,
regional, and global problems in classrooms, schools, and out-of school civic contexts.

068765B3C7D64D71A13BE3E51B0463B4.description:
Analyze the characteristics and causation of local, regional, and global problems issues
using a multidisciplinary lens.

E2B90D773D164E76B24A7536655C6D7A.description:
Present arguments and explanations that feature evocative ideas and multiple
perspectives about political issues and topics to reach a range of audiences and venues
outside the classroom using print, oral, and digital technologies.

FD6B90E7DE7846E3BE3F1F82280DBEB1.description:
Critique political arguments and explanations while acknowledging the strengths and
weaknesses given the purpose and audience (credibility, bias, reasoning, sequencing,
details).

CAEDFF82F16C4B4CBFFF383107BF9382.description:
Construct explanations using sound reasoning, correct sequence, relevant examples,
and pertinent details to contextualize evidence and arguments (e.g., chronology,
causation, procedure).

3C953C10BB0349ABB888A35C8E3D39DE.description:
Construct arguments using precise and knowledgeable claims, with evidence from
multiple sources, while acknowledging counterclaims and evidentiary weaknesses.

Refine claims and counterclaims by pointing out strengths and limitations of arguments

Organize and prioritize evidence directly and substantively from multiple sources in

8FC8F2C0CF5B4FE98D7832CBC9F6B7B2.description:
Gather relevant information from multiple sources representing a wide range of views
and mediums while using the origin, authority, structure, context, and corroborative
value to guide the selection of credible sources.

D3C8AA330C194F1F9139706FA66C1108.description:

DE0F0EAF9F4045BFA9BA9971E519C90D.description:
Novice learners can set language learning goals appropriate
to their proficiency level and reflect upon their progress toward
meeting their goal.

A92830D64B264979B8E4837B535A0779.description: Lifelong Learning Performance Descriptors: Learners set goals and reflect on their progress in using language for enjoyment, enrichment, and advancement.

70F6E4C23A3D4BDB900405394208F416.description:
Novice learners can use the target language, with support and
scaffolding, to connect and interact with members of their local
and global community on topics related to themselves, with
cultural competence and understanding.

62AB442A29C348BF966E17AFEF857AD8.description: School and Global Communities Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language both within and beyond the classroom to interact and collaborate in their community and the globalized world.

0B9D9646651E41ACACCBC55DD5E46644.description:
COMMUNITIES: Learners communicate and interact with cultural competence to
participate in multilingual communities at home and around the world.

785001CB30BA47948F9BAFCDD69EE505.description:
Novice learners can investigate the concept of culture through
comparisons of the language culture(s) and their own.

52EE84793CD7491A88E4A665E6EC99A3.description:
Cultural Comparisons Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language to investigate, explain,
and reflect on the concept of culture through comparisons of the cultures studied and their own.

D193723A26AE48168F84F921D20D840B.description: Novice learners can investigate the nature and structure of language through comparisons of the language studied and their own.

E74E7BBE3CC940C0897EE3A078903C3A.description:
Language Comparisons Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language to investigate, reflect on,
and explain the nature of language through comparisons of the language studied and their own.

0D0AE8192FDC454D89A49F291567CECB.description: COMPARISONS: Learners develop insight into the nature of language and culture to interact with cultural competence.

269162E5BCA340D593559949256BB903.description:
Novice learners can recognize diverse perspectives and distinctive viewpoints on very familiar common daily topics, primarily in
the target language, from age-appropriate authentic materials
from the communities where the language is spoken.

CA0A35281C9B49C58CE14473DE09306C.description:
Acquiring Information and Diverse Perspectives Performance Descriptors:
Learners access and evaluate information and diverse perspectives that are available through the language and its cultures.

BB6E43D721B641E9B29C20006D5B58E6.description:
Novice learners can acquire, exchange, and present information
primarily in the target language about very familiar common
daily elements of life and age-appropriate academic content
across disciplines.

A27BD07856FC41C6A46292A9F75AC2E0.description:
Making Connections Performance Descriptors: Learners build, reinforce, and expand their knowledge
of other disciplines while using the language to develop critical thinking and to solve problems creatively.

8ECC395EB28643A1A477B0079D2A860B.description:
CONNECTIONS: Learners connect with other disciplines and acquire information and diverse perspectives
in order to use the language to function in academic- and career-related situations.

9BFCCB5DCCA44933B5054849492BCFF8.description:
Novice learners can identify products to help them understand
perspectives in their own and other cultures.

DECAAC517D6B45FC9C51852850F4FAC4.description:
Relating Cultural Products to Perspectives Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language to investigate,
explain, and reflect on the relationship between the products and perspectives of the cultures studied.

485C0DEF8A354E79B1660922766A98AB.description:
Novice learners can identify practices to help them understand
perspectives in their own and other cultures.

874635B613D248918B210DAAFA698FEC.description:
Relating Cultural Practices to Perspectives Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language to investigate,
explain, and reflect on the relationship between the practices and perspectives of the cultures studied.

D5B84313C5264B57B85B968E22576A6B.description: CULTURES: Learners interact with cultural competence and understanding.

886E54F4142149F5A195DA1EAB6EE1B3.description:
Novice High learners
can present basic information about themselves and familiar
topics using language
they have practiced
using memorized
phrases, simple sentences, and sometimes
creating meaning with
language they know.

5FDA976D15FA416C8B919D83B84C1717.description:
Novice Mid learners
can present
information about
themselves and some
other very familiar
topics using practiced
words, phrases, and
memorized expressions.

8E2257EDE51C45ECB5B73C7D908798A1.description:
Novice Low learners
can present
information about
themselves and some
other very familiar
topics using practiced
words or memorized
phrases with the help of
gestures or visuals.

8281337717C043E6AF394EE8F97F3BC7.description:
Presentational Communication Performance Descriptors: Learners present spoken, written, or signed information, concepts, and ideas to inform, explain,
persuade, and narrate on a variety of topics using appropriate media and adapting to various audiences of listeners, readers, or viewers.

D8E44261BC4E4C51B0232331A94E0C72.description:
Novice High learners
can identify the topic
and some facts from
simple sentences, and
understand simple
questions on familiar
topics that they hear,
read, and view.

2E60BE9ABEF349EC864D74B8A65E51FF.description:
Novice Mid learners
can identify some basic
facts from memorized
words or phrases that
are supported by gestures or visuals on topics related to everyday
life that they hear, read,
and view.

3FBAC04EA1E14AFE9201FF2153127587.description:
Novice Low learners
can identify memorized or familiar words
that are supported
by gestures or visuals
related to everyday life
that they hear, read,
and view.

1E42982D3A2341A5A88A054EFB3F0258.description: Interpretive Communication Performance Descriptors: Learners understand, interpret, and analyze what is heard, read, or viewed on a variety of topics.

1027F41DED9643B3854025E5ECB24121.description:
Novice High learners
can communicate
and exchange information about familiar
topics using phrases
and simple memorized
sentences. They can
usually handle short
social interactions in
everyday situations by
asking and answering
simple, sometimes original questions.

FFA3E4E5AB46405E9778EF0F52FA7811.description:
Novice Mid learners
can communicate on
very familiar topics
using a variety of words
and phrases that they
have practiced and
memorized.

3D1F5224883C49F5B992D94745FDE91A.description:
Novice Low learners
can communicate
on some very familiar
topics using simple and
memorized words and
phrases with support of
gestures and visuals.

ECCE89E91BE0480693E3C5153815F836.description:
Interpersonal Communication Performance Descriptors: Learners interact and negotiate meaning in
spoken, signed, or written conversations to share information, reactions, feelings, and opinions.

A2B4D22A03034D2CAC3AEC1BC0356BE8.description: COMMUNICATION: Learners can communicate effectively in more than one language to function in a variety of situations and for multiple purposes.

document.title: Connecticut K-12 World Language Standards 2024

555D28F7DE19407AA7CD9692812696EC.description:
Intermediate learners can set language learning goals appropriate
to their proficiency level, and goals for personal enjoyment and
enrichment, and reflect on their progress toward meeting their goal(s).

DC74A1136B8148EA88FC3168E38B7AA7.description: Lifelong Learning Performance Descriptors: Learners set goals and reflect on their progress in using language for enjoyment, enrichment, and advancement.

CE2BF89D9253450196F95A656BF02DB2.description:
Intermediate learners can use the target language to connect
and interact with members of their local, state, national, and global
communities on topics related to themselves and familiar topics
with cultural competence and understanding in order to participate
in multilingual communities at home.

68956EB95957418CADEEEE2ED35B516E.description: School and Global Communities Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language both within and beyond the classroom to interact and collaborate in their community and the globalized world.

21B52158AA36436D8F163F59EDD55086.description:
COMMUNITIES: Learners communicate and interact with cultural competence to
participate in multilingual communities at home and around the world.

F42FE15C2BBC4355B24CBAF510B88B1A.description:
Intermediate learners can investigate and explain the concept of
culture through comparisons of the language culture(s) and their
own.

BC20B346221240F290B817ED6631F575.description:
Cultural Comparisons Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language to investigate, explain,
and reflect on the concept of culture through comparisons of the cultures studied and their own.

D8C68BF13C9D4318A330D0B6D35A9A78.description:
Intermediate learners can investigate and reflect on the nature
and structure of language through comparisons of the language
studied and their own.

DDA6B72CE9D4468C9585D0D6FF4FF025.description:
Language Comparisons Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language to investigate, reflect on,
and explain the nature of language through comparisons of the language studied and their own.

FEE19ECC656B44A896C8DAC6E3433ECC.description: COMPARISONS: Learners develop insight into the nature of language and culture to interact with cultural competence.

65E505F049FB4C188D4D5A17FCF60BB8.description:
Intermediate learners can identify diverse perspectives and
distinctive viewpoints on topics related to self and the immediate
environment in the target language from age-appropriate authentic
materials from the communities where the language is spoken.

25BD1FF8EFA949EA9AD3066C2FE18C5B.description:
Acquiring Information and Diverse Perspectives Performance Descriptors:
Learners access and evaluate information and diverse perspectives that are available through the language and its cultures.

B8DD0E3B28034D36823650C5504EB0A0.description:
Intermediate learners can acquire, exchange, and present
information in the target language on topics related to self and the
immediate environment and age-appropriate academic content
across disciplines.

FC4344736F294822BF4414CA073B0B75.description:
Making Connections Performance Descriptors: Learners build, reinforce, and expand their knowledge
of other disciplines while using the language to develop critical thinking and to solve problems creatively.

E5D56B8898774582A3F6CC269625AD52.description:
CONNECTIONS: Learners connect with other disciplines and acquire information and diverse perspectives
in order to use the language to function in academic- and career-related situations.

27CB6B9AE0A145D6A34FEF58F1DEBBB7.description:
Intermediate learners can identify and compare products to help
them understand perspectives in their own and other cultures.

2B84FA3827D74147958C6B2791929311.description:
Relating Cultural Products to Perspectives Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language to investigate,
explain, and reflect on the relationship between the products and perspectives of the cultures studied.

1CEF12E61D08455C82938E1D5EA8E944.description:
Intermediate learners can identify and compare practices to help
them understand perspectives in their own and other cultures.

0AA5E282A69B43B1B0C153E4BAE10F83.description:
Relating Cultural Practices to Perspectives Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language to investigate,
explain, and reflect on the relationship between the practices and perspectives of the cultures studied.

B4BD8EDBFD774339AA15687BDFE97616.description: CULTURES: Learners interact with cultural competence and understanding.

71036627DC4A4F46AC8DDF966E96A1E6.description:
Intermediate High
learners can present
information in a generally organized way
on school, work, and
community topics, and
on topics they have
researched. They can
make presentations
on some events and
experiences in various
time frames.

166A05F980894017B7DF5D726ACDB0C0.description:
Intermediate Mid
learners can make
written, spoken or
signed presentations
on a wide variety of
familiar topics using
connected sentences
with detail.

FF5F77CF8F754EA6916A8EE425EB9D78.description:
Intermediate Low
learners can present
information in a written,
spoken, or signed
format on most familiar
topics using a series of
self-created sentences
with some detail.

FA85472D66E84A6AAF4868C69F250AFD.description:
Presentational Communication Performance Descriptors: Learners present spoken, written, or signed information, concepts, and ideas to inform, explain,
persuade, and narrate on a variety of topics using appropriate media and adapting to various audiences of listeners, readers, or viewers.

94B4D4A144A84C3798236014727FBF82.description:
Intermediate High
learners can easily
understand the main
idea in messages, texts,
and presentations
on a variety of topics
related to everyday
life, personal interests,
and their studies.
They can understand
some details of what
they hear, even when
something unexpected
is expressed.

B2F1631B4FFA45C1B7EB6F253C4EB6BE.description:
Intermediate Mid
learners can understand the main idea in
messages and presentations on a variety of
topics related to everyday life and personal
interests and studies.
They can understand
the main idea in conversations, and understand the main idea of
texts related to everyday life and personal
interests or studies.

F7F191D5EC624F959EE0CA941C88EE59.description:
Intermediate Low
learners can understand the main idea
and details in messages and presentations on
a variety of topics related to everyday life and
personal interests and
studies. They can understand the main idea
of simple conversations,
and understand the
main idea of short and
simple texts when the
topic is familiar.

99D5B3BDF7C24D0EB3BBA1D42DDB3B56.description: Interpretive Communication Performance Descriptors: Learners understand, interpret, and analyze what is heard, read, or viewed on a variety of topics.

4D5A4C598EE441F3BEBB674F3940396A.description:
Intermediate High learners can participate with
ease and confidence in
conversations on familiar
or researched topics.
They can usually talk
about events and experiences in various time
frames. They can usually
describe people, places,
and things. They can
handle social interactions
in everyday situations,
sometimes even when
there is an unexpected
complication.

5F6A5F18A9E043FFA663301386273CA1.description:
Intermediate Mid
learners can participate
in conversations on
familiar topics using
sentences and series
of sentences. They can
handle short social
interactions in everyday
situations by asking
and answering a variety
of questions. They can
usually say what they
want to say about
themselves and their
everyday lives.

57096503D9854DAABCCF5251F52AECF0.description:
Intermediate Low
learners can participate
in conversations on
a number of familiar
topics using simple
sentences and
sometimes creating
original sentences. They
can handle short social
interactions in everyday
situations by asking
and answering simple
questions.

85EB3B9E48FE47F1975C26F3F44FDE68.description:
Interpersonal Communication Performance Descriptors: Learners interact and negotiate meaning in
spoken, signed, or written conversations to share information, reactions, feelings, and opinions.

314BBFA0F8AF4B10BCD639BAA41C1E05.description: COMMUNICATION: Learners can communicate effectively in more than one language to function in a variety of situations and for multiple purposes.

document.title: Connecticut K-12 World Language Standards 2024

3F25A947D4014E0FAD7C3607A38D67EC.description:
Advanced learners can set goals appropriate to their proficiency
level, for personal enjoyment and enrichment, and reflect upon
their journey and how the language has enriched and enlivened
their life.

2B4EBE319ABD4687BFFF236F061501E4.description: Lifelong Learning Performance Descriptors: Learners set goals and reflect on their progress in using language for enjoyment, enrichment, and advancement.

6FC9AE6EC3B4450E8324F2075A932386.description:
Advanced learners can use the target language to connect
and interact with members of their local, state, national, and
global communities on topics of general public interest with
cultural competence and understanding in order to participate
in multilingual communities at home and around the world.

2F48292AAAE54BE8A2D162E4F0B5B5CD.description: School and Global Communities Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language both within and beyond the classroom to interact and collaborate in their community and the globalized world.

4205EBA3AE79411686666C91402C633E.description:
COMMUNITIES: Learners communicate and interact with cultural competence to
participate in multilingual communities at home and around the world.

E96A3B9719914419BB868B661E531A6E.description:
Advanced learners can investigate, explain, and reflect on
the concept of culture through comparisons of the language
culture(s) and their own.

CC353076979F445E87CEA2B01A3D6CC5.description:
Cultural Comparisons Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language to investigate, explain,
and reflect on the concept of culture through comparisons of the cultures studied and their own.

CC8BA31C5863456FB55EE4D92480E9DE.description:
Advanced learners can investigate, reflect on, and explain the
nature and structure of language through comparisons of the
language studied and their own.

1FC9682771EE4FC2BD739673BD10DF78.description:
Language Comparisons Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language to investigate, reflect on,
and explain the nature of language through comparisons of the language studied and their own.

60A73E99817643EAA76344234E8873FB.description: COMPARISONS: Learners develop insight into the nature of language and culture to interact with cultural competence.

BD50ED8D7B1E4E4F92FD7BABBE4A3CB6.description:
Advanced learners can research and explain diverse perspectives
and distinctive viewpoints on topics of public interest and general
academic content in the target language through authentic
materials from the communities where the language is spoken.

51E17B5E0C9A4E8EB55D3822E4C648BF.description:
Acquiring Information and Diverse Perspectives Performance Descriptors:
Learners access and evaluate information and diverse perspectives that are available through the language and its cultures.

E7DCE9741334426499B1F0A2E708DDC5.description:
Advanced learners can acquire, exchange, and present
information in the target language on factual topics of public
interest and general academic content across disciplines.

974F02E0D15E4C2AB56B21B215546099.description:
Making Connections Performance Descriptors: Learners build, reinforce, and expand their knowledge
of other disciplines while using the language to develop critical thinking and to solve problems creatively.

AEE9438C42F44F02826702D0F45D8439.description:
CONNECTIONS: Learners connect with other disciplines and acquire information and diverse perspectives
in order to use the language to function in academic- and career-related situations.

50ACA5CADDDD4ED192A128B6B26F5D52.description:
Advanced learners can identify, compare, and explain products to
help them understand perspectives in their own and other cultures.

DC3431AAE9F44F83B177CA5C2B10CA53.description:
Relating Cultural Products to Perspectives Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language to investigate,
explain, and reflect on the relationship between the products and perspectives of the cultures studied.

83BA8110DD7441818321601A1B343019.description:
Advanced learners can identify, compare, and explain practices to
help them understand perspectives in their own and other cultures.

24508D6861D0460F82C9A68C9DDB58F3.description:
Relating Cultural Practices to Perspectives Performance Descriptors: Learners use the language to investigate,
explain, and reflect on the relationship between the practices and perspectives of the cultures studied.

26113445C546423889DEB9EC0EDFF73B.description: CULTURES: Learners interact with cultural competence and understanding.

E9293D71823C4B3B8BA73EAC2C87099E.description:
Advanced High
learners can deliver
detailed written or
spoken presentations,
with accuracy, clarity,
and precision on a
variety of topics and
issues related to
community interests
and some special fields
of expertise.

3AEA77AB3A764275B9D04F06728E58DF.description:
Advanced Mid learners
can deliver wellorganized written or
spoken presentations
on concrete social,
academic, and
professional topics. They
can present detailed
information about
events and experiences
in various time frames.

A1605D544709440FBEE7B6AF3EA933E4.description:
Advanced Low
learners can deliver
organized written or
spoken presentations
appropriate to their
audience on a variety
of topics. They can
present information
about events and
experiences in various
time frames.

D36D3C400706482FA08A71D35908E066.description:
Presentational Communication Performance Descriptors: Learners present spoken, written, or signed information, concepts, and ideas to inform, explain,
persuade, and narrate on a variety of topics using appropriate media and adapting to various audiences of listeners, readers, or viewers.

CA5C2279F7A74BA79EB54588AB21BBE0.description:
Advanced High learners can understand,
with ease, narrative,
informational, and
descriptive speech and
texts. They can understand most topics
that deal with special
interests, unfamiliar
situations, and abstract
concepts. They can
sometimes follow extended arguments and
different points of view.

A63F2EA8635E431BA1E1BA4216A2053D.description:
Advanced Mid learners
can understand the main
idea and most supporting detail on a variety of
topics of personal and
general interest, as well
as some topics of professional interest. They
can follow stories and
descriptions in various
time frames. They can
understand information presented in most
genres, even when not
familiar with the topic.

05D0BE79E236459BBFAC1DD507FFCD30.description:
Advanced Low learners
can understand the
main idea and some
supporting details on
a variety of topics of
personal and general
interest. They can follow
stories and descriptions
in various time frames.
They can understand
information presented
in a variety of genres
on familiar topics, even
when something unexpected is expressed.

EC565E965268419AAEA9FD0E4D42D36A.description: Interpretive Communication Performance Descriptors: Learners understand, interpret, and analyze what is heard, read, or viewed on a variety of topics.

14A9ADE5F47D4A859778F367521D1C68.description:
Advanced High
learners can express
themselves freely
and spontaneously,
and for the most part
accurately, on concrete
topics and on most
complex issues. They
can usually support
their opinion and
develop hypotheses
on topics of particular
interest or personal
expertise.

128E21ED09FE434583D8AC9F6B1674D7.description:
Advanced Mid
learners can express
themselves fully not only
on familiar topics but
also on some concrete
social, academic, and
professional topics. They
can talk in detail and in
an organized way about
events and experiences in
various time frames, and
share their points of view
on complex issues. They
can confidently handle
routine situations with an
unexpected complication.

BB872861159045B59A2D55F0A3E22882.description:
Advanced Low learners can participate in
conversations about
familiar topics that go
beyond their everyday
lives. They can talk in
an organized way with
some detail about
events and experiences
in various time frames.
They can describe people, places, and things
in an organized way
with some detail. They
can handle a familiar
situation with an unexpected complication.

4C735AFCCB7846558EF7244D807BFF52.description:
Interpersonal Communication Performance Descriptors: Learners interact and negotiate meaning in
spoken, signed, or written conversations to share information, reactions, feelings, and opinions.

E4004498E77649358F83C2A693001867.description: COMMUNICATION: Learners can communicate effectively in more than one language to function in a variety of situations and for multiple purposes.
